profiles.name: Core CPI
profiles.short_description: Consumer prices excluding food and energy.
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in prices paid by urban consumers for a basket of goods and services, excluding the volatile food and energy categories.
profiles.why_it_matters: It is the market’s main read on underlying inflation momentum; a single 0.1 percentage-point miss can move rate expectations.
profiles.release_frequency: Monthly, about two weeks after the reference month
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Direct measure of underlying consumer inflation.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Indirect: persistent inflation can squeeze real incomes and spending.
profiles.relationship_to_labor_market: Services inflation is closely tied to wage growth.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: The Fed targets 2% PCE inflation, but CPI arrives first and shapes expectations for PCE and the rate path.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Core m/m versus consensus (0.1 pp matters), the 3-month annualized pace, shelter, and supercore.

profiles.name: CPI
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in prices for the full consumer basket, including food and energy.
profiles.why_it_matters: Headline inflation drives inflation expectations and real income; markets usually weigh core more heavily.
profiles.release_frequency: Monthly, about two weeks after the reference month
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Energy spikes can act like a tax on consumers.
profiles.relationship_to_labor_market: Indirect, through wage-setting and inflation expectations.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Relevant to the Fed mainly through its influence on expectations and on the PCE estimate.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Headline versus core divergence, energy contribution, year-over-year trend.

profiles.name: Core PCE Price Index
profiles.short_description: The Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of underlying inflation.
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in prices of personal consumption expenditures excluding food and energy, with weights based on what consumers actually spend.
profiles.why_it_matters: The Fed’s 2% inflation objective is defined on PCE; core PCE is its main gauge of underlying trend.
profiles.release_frequency: Monthly, near the end of the following month
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: The official inflation benchmark for monetary policy.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Released with personal income and spending, which describe consumer demand.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Most directly tied to the Fed’s mandate; persistent deviations from 2% shape the rate path.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Core m/m versus consensus; often partly anticipated from CPI and PPI, so surprises can be smaller.

profiles.name: PCE Price Index
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in prices of all personal consumption expenditures.
profiles.why_it_matters: The Fed’s 2% target is defined on headline PCE, though policy discussion focuses on core.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Headline inflation benchmark for the Fed target.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Referenced in the Fed’s statement and projections.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Year-over-year headline versus the 2% target; personal spending in the same release.

profiles.name: Core PPI
profiles.short_description: Producer prices excluding food and energy.
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in selling prices received by domestic producers, excluding food and energy.
profiles.why_it_matters: A read on pipeline price pressure; some components feed directly into PCE estimates.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Upstream inflation; can foreshadow consumer prices.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Margin components reflect business pricing power.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Matters mainly through its implications for the core PCE estimate.
profiles.typical_market_focus: PCE-relevant components more than the headline number.

profiles.name: PPI
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in prices received by domestic producers for their output (final demand).
profiles.why_it_matters: Signals cost pressures that may pass through to consumers.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Secondary to CPI and PCE, but used to refine PCE estimates.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Services components, and how PCE-mapped items move.

profiles.name: Nonfarm Payrolls
profiles.what_it_measures: Net change in the number of payroll jobs outside farming, from the establishment survey of employers.
profiles.why_it_matters: The headline labor-market report; it tests both sides of the Fed’s mandate and often produces large moves.
profiles.releasing_agency: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) — Employment Situation
important_components: Revisions to the two prior months
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Through wages: strong hiring can sustain services inflation.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Employment growth supports income and spending.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: A cooling labor market can support easier policy; strong hiring can reduce the urgency to cut.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Headline versus consensus, revisions, unemployment rate and wages together.

profiles.name: Unemployment Rate
profiles.short_description: Share of the labor force without a job.
profiles.what_it_measures: Percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively looking for work, from the household survey.
profiles.why_it_matters: Directly tied to the Fed’s maximum-employment mandate; rises can shift the policy outlook quickly.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Indirect: a tighter labor market can support wage and price growth.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Rising unemployment can signal slowing activity.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Compared with the Fed’s projections; unexpected rises can raise expectations of cuts.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Change versus prior month and versus Fed projections; participation.

profiles.name: Average Hourly Earnings
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in average hourly earnings of private-sector employees.
profiles.why_it_matters: Wage growth is a key driver of services inflation.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Faster wage growth can sustain services inflation.
profiles.typical_market_focus: m/m versus 0.3%; year-over-year trend; composition effects.

profiles.name: Initial Jobless Claims
profiles.what_it_measures: Number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time in the reporting week.
profiles.why_it_matters: The most timely labor-market indicator; trends can signal layoffs before monthly data.
profiles.relationship_to_growth: Rising claims can indicate slowing activity.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: A sustained rise can shift the Fed toward easier policy.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Trend and 4-week average rather than one week; holiday and seasonal noise.

profiles.name: ADP Employment Change
profiles.what_it_measures: Change in private-sector employment estimated from ADP payroll-processing data.
profiles.why_it_matters: Arrives two days before the official report; watched as a partial signal, though it often diverges from payrolls.
profiles.release_frequency: Monthly, Wednesday before the Employment Situation
profiles.releasing_agency: ADP Research with Stanford Digital Economy Lab
important_components: Private employment by size and sector
Pay growth for job-stayers and job-changers
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Pay data gives a read on wage pressure.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Limited on its own; relevant through expectations for payrolls.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Surprise versus consensus; historically an imperfect predictor of nonfarm payrolls.

profiles.name: JOLTS Job Openings
profiles.what_it_measures: Number of job openings on the last business day of the reference month, with hires, quits and layoffs.
profiles.why_it_matters: A read on labor demand and churn; quits relate to wage pressure.
profiles.release_frequency: Monthly, about five weeks after the reference month
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Quits and openings relate to wage pressure.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Openings versus consensus, quits rate trend.

profiles.name: GDP
profiles.what_it_measures: Annualized quarter-over-quarter growth in real gross domestic product.
profiles.why_it_matters: The broadest measure of activity; advance estimates can shift growth expectations.
profiles.release_frequency: Quarterly: advance, second and third estimates
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: The deflator and core PCE for the quarter are included.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Influences the growth side of the outlook; weak growth can support easier policy.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Final sales to private domestic purchasers; inventory and trade distortions.

profiles.name: Retail Sales
profiles.what_it_measures: Month-over-month change in the value of sales at retail and food-service stores (not inflation-adjusted).
profiles.why_it_matters: Consumer spending drives most of the U.S. economy.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Nominal: part of the change can be price increases.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Strong demand can reduce the urgency to ease.

profiles.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
profiles.what_it_measures: Diffusion index from purchasing managers; above 50 indicates expansion, below 50 contraction.
profiles.why_it_matters: Timely read on the industrial cycle and price pressures.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Prices paid is an early signal of goods inflation.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Secondary, but prices paid can influence inflation expectations.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Headline versus 50 and consensus; new orders; prices paid.

profiles.name: ISM Services PMI
profiles.what_it_measures: Diffusion index from services purchasing managers; above 50 indicates expansion.
profiles.why_it_matters: Services dominate the U.S. economy and services inflation is sticky.
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Prices paid relates to services inflation.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Watched for inflation persistence in services.

profiles.name: CB Consumer Confidence
profiles.what_it_measures: Index of consumers’ assessment of current conditions and expectations from the Conference Board.
profiles.why_it_matters: A soft read on household mood; the labor-market differential is watched.
important_components: Jobs plentiful vs hard to get
profiles.typical_market_focus: Expectations index and labor differential rather than the headline.

profiles.match: (interest rate decision|rate decision|fomc statement|federal funds|fed press conference|press conference)
profiles.name: FOMC Rate Decision
profiles.what_it_measures: The target range for the federal funds rate set by the Federal Open Market Committee, with the policy statement; quarterly meetings include economic projections and the dot plot.
profiles.why_it_matters: Sets the price of money; the statement, projections and press conference can reprice the entire rate path.
profiles.release_frequency: Eight scheduled meetings per year; statement at 2:00 PM ET, press conference at 2:30 PM ET
profiles.typical_market_focus: Surprise versus market pricing, statement changes, dot plot, and the chair’s tone.

profiles.name: FOMC Meeting Minutes
profiles.short_description: Record of the previous Fed meeting.
profiles.what_it_measures: Detailed summary of the discussion at the FOMC meeting held three weeks earlier.
profiles.why_it_matters: Adds nuance on how many participants lean toward easing or tightening.
profiles.release_frequency: Three weeks after each meeting, 2:00 PM ET
profiles.relationship_to_inflation: Shows how officials weigh inflation risks.
profiles.relationship_to_fed_policy: Clarifies the reaction function behind the last decision.
profiles.typical_market_focus: Wording on the direction and pace of policy; number of participants holding each view.
